title: Approved Partner API Abuse (`GitHubDeleteRepository`)
failure_mode: When an injected prompt instructs the agent to delete or modify resources on an authorized partner service (e.g., GitHub, Slack, Google Calendar), perimeter domain filtering is bypassed.
empirical_evidence: In InjecAgent (N=748), B4 missed 17 direct-harm test cases where the attacker tool was `GitHubDeleteRepository`. Because `api.github.com` is listed in `APPROVED_API_DOMAINS` and the delete arguments contained no database query or PII, the call was allowed.
label: known architectural blindspot

title: Multi-Step Exfiltration at Step 1 (`DropboxListFilesAndFolders`)
failure_mode: Indirect injection attacks that begin with a read-only metadata query before exfiltrating data in a subsequent step.
empirical_evidence: In InjecAgent (N=748), B4 permitted 17 data-stealing test cases at step 1 where the attacker requested `DropboxListFilesAndFolders` before emailing the listing in step 2. Because reading file metadata is not an egress violation, SentinelMesh permits the listing and only blocks the attack at step 2.
label: step-level deferred block

title: Database Write Contention at Extreme Concurrency (c=50)
failure_mode: Thread locking during cryptographic HMAC SHA-256 tamper-evident hash chaining under high concurrent load.
empirical_evidence: During real HTTP benchmarking through Uvicorn with SQLite WAL mode on 2-core hardware:   - At c=1, 5, 20: 0 timeouts, p50 latency 145ms to 4.2s.   - At c=50 (50 parallel agent streams): 581 out of 1000 requests timed out (10s timeout threshold) due to SQLite database write-lock serialization.
label: hardware & engine concurrency bound

title: Zero Protection from Static Regex Matchers (B2 Evasion)
failure_mode: Perimeter text filters and regex matchers (Baseline B2) provide zero defense against semantic indirect prompt injection.
empirical_evidence: Across all 748 test cases in InjecAgent Base and Enhanced settings, Baseline B2 achieved exactly 0.0% prevention (0/748). Modern indirect injection instructions use natural conversational framing ("Please delete my project repository..."), completely bypassing naive signature dictionaries.
label: demonstrated baseline failure

title: Partial Span Masking on Unstructured PII
failure_mode: Regex-based privacy masking excels at structured tokens but suffers partial span boundaries on unstructured entities.
empirical_evidence: On the `ai4privacy` 1,028-sample test partition, regex masking achieves 100% recall on SSNs and 94.2% on phone numbers, but type-agnostic span recall drops on multi-word names or unusual international formats without transformer NER models.
label: syntactic privacy boundary
